definition_zh: 数学家；数学工作者；（旧时）占星术士
definition_en: a person who studies or works in mathematics; in earlier English, also a person who practised astrology
core_image: 书房里，一位研究者面前只有几张写满符号的纸，墙上小黑板还留着一条待证的命题
scene: 书房里，一位研究者面前的纸上只有符号与箭头，墙上的小黑板写着一个还没证完的命题。The mathematician worked for six years before the proof was accepted.
sceneCN: 这里 mathematician 指「以研究数学为业的人」（第 1 个义项：从事数学研究的人）；句意为这位数学家做了六年，证明才被接受。图中可辨识物件：草稿纸、符号、小黑板、铅笔。

pos.zh: 数学家；数学研究者
（十六、十七世纪用法）占星术士

senses.title: A researcher in mathematics
senses.definition: a person whose profession is to study or advance mathematics
senses.definitionCN: 以研究或推进数学为职业的人
senses.example: The mathematician worked for six years before the proof was accepted.
senses.exampleCN: 这位数学家做了六年，证明才被接受。
senses.why: The person suffix turns the field's name into the name of someone who works in it.
senses.whyCN: 表人后缀把学科之名变成从事该学科者之名。

senses.title: A teacher of the subject
senses.titleCN: 数学教师与数学工作者
senses.definition: a person who teaches mathematics or applies it as part of a job
senses.definitionCN: 教授数学、或在工作中的一部分运用数学的人
senses.example: The school hired a mathematician to run the advanced class.
senses.exampleCN: 学校聘请了一位数学工作者来带高级班。
senses.why: Teaching and applied work both count as living by the subject, so the word covers more than research alone.
senses.whyCN: 教书与应用工作都算靠这门学问谋生，因此这个词的覆盖面大于纯研究。

senses.title: Someone good with numbers
senses.titleCN: 擅长计算的人（宽泛说法）
senses.definition: used loosely of anyone unusually skilled at calculation
senses.definitionCN: 宽松地指任何在计算上特别熟练的人
senses.example: You do not need to be a mathematician to check that bill.
senses.exampleCN: 核对那张账单并不需要你是数学家。
senses.why: Everyday speech uses the word as a compliment for number sense, without insisting on formal training.
senses.whyCN: 日常说法用这个词称赞数字感，并不要求受过正式训练。

senses.title: A specialist in one branch
senses.definition: a person expert in a particular branch, such as geometry or number theory
senses.definitionCN: 精通某一分支（如几何或数论）的人
senses.example: The geometer and the analyst were both mathematicians, but they read different journals.
senses.exampleCN: 几何学家与分析学家都是数学家，但读的期刊不同。
senses.why: Branch names describe narrower expertise while the general word still applies to all of them.
senses.whyCN: 分支名称描述更窄的专长，而通名仍适用于其中所有人。

senses.title: A historical author of mathematical works
senses.titleCN: 历史上撰写数学著作的人
senses.definition: a historical figure known for written mathematical work rather than for a modern post
senses.definitionCN: 以数学著述而非现代职位闻名的历史人物
senses.example: The mathematician left a single book that was read for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这位数学家只留下一本书，却被读了几个世纪。
senses.why: History remembers people by their books, so the word attaches to authorship as much as to employment.
senses.whyCN: 历史按著作记住人，因此这个词既指职业，也指著述身份。

senses.title: An astrologer, in older usage
senses.definition: in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, a person who cast horoscopes and calculated celestial positions
senses.definitionCN: 在十六、十七世纪，指推算星盘与天体位置的人
senses.example: In Shakespeare's day a mathematician might be paid to read the stars.
senses.exampleCN: 在莎士比亚的时代，「数学家」可能受雇去读星象。
senses.why: Astronomy and astrology were then one body of calculation, and whoever did that calculation carried the name.
senses.whyCN: 当时天文与占星是一套计算，做这套计算的人便带着这个名号。

senses.title: A modeller in industry
senses.titleCN: 工业与金融中的数学建模人员
senses.definition: a person employed to build mathematical models for practical decisions
senses.definitionCN: 受雇为实际决策建立数学模型的人
senses.example: The insurer's mathematicians priced the new policy.
senses.exampleCN: 这家保险公司的数学人员为新保单定了价。
senses.why: Outside academia the same training is sold as modelling, and the old word follows the skill.
senses.whyCN: 在学界之外，同样的训练以建模之名出售，旧词随技能而行。

senses.title: A calculating person, figuratively
senses.definition: used of someone who plans every move as if solving an equation
senses.definitionCN: 比喻把每一步都当作解方程来筹划的人
senses.example: A good negotiator is something of a mathematician about other people's motives.
senses.exampleCN: 好的谈判者对他人动机的把握颇有几分数学家的味道。
senses.why: The figurative use transfers the cool step-by-step manner of proof to social behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 比喻用法把证明中那种冷静的逐步骤态度移用到社交行为上。

intro.en: The word is the name of the field plus a suffix for a person. Its Greek root means 'learning', and its early English sense could include astrology. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词由学科之名加表人后缀构成。其希腊词根意为「学习」，早期英语中还可指占星。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mathēma 'something learned' came from manthanein 'to learn'; the deeper root is reconstructed, not attested.
items.cn: mathēma「所学之物」源自动词 manthanein「学习」；更深词根属重构形式，并无实证。

items.en: Latin mathematicus named a student of the mathematical studies, and in later usage could also mean an astrologer.
items.cn: 拉丁 mathematicus 指数学诸科的研习者，后世也可指占星者。

items.en: Sixteenth-century English used mathematic for the field itself, and the person's name was formed from it.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语用 mathematic 指这门学问本身，表人之名即由此构成。

items.en: The ending came into English through French from Latin -ianus, which marks someone connected with a thing.
items.cn: 这个表人词尾经法语来自拉丁 -ianus，标记与某事物有关联的人。

items.en: Because celestial prediction was then a branch of calculation, a mathematician could be hired to cast a horoscope; the sense faded as the two trades separated.
items.cn: 由于当时星象预测属于计算的一支，「数学家」可受雇推算星盘；随着两种行业分开，这一义项衰落。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word settled on the academic and industrial researcher. First date uncertain: no single year is recorded for the narrower modern sense.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个词固定指学术与工业中的研究者。首见年代不确定：较窄的现代义没有确切年份记录。

note.en: Group one separates words that look alike but belong to different roots; group two separates the neighbouring specialists.
note.cn: 第一组辨析外形相近而词根不同的词；第二组辨析相邻的专门从业者。

entries.definition: An older adjective and singular noun for the field; it never names a person, though it looks like a shortened form of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 更早的形容词与单数名词，指这门学问；它从不指人，尽管看起来像本词的缩短形式。

entries.definition: Describes work or ability rather than a person; 'a mathematical person' is not the same as 'a mathematician'.
entries.definitionCN: 描述工作或能力，而不指人；「有数学头脑的人」与「数学家」并不等同。

entries.definition: A person skilled in arithmetic, built on the Greek word for number rather than on the word for learning.
entries.definitionCN: 指精通算术的人，建立在希腊语表示数字的词上，而非表示学习的词上。

entries.definition: A specialist in geometry; the branch name plus the person suffix, parallel in form but narrower in scope.
entries.definitionCN: 指几何学专家；分支名加表人后缀，形式平行而范围更窄。

entries.definition: One who works mainly with symbolic equations; a mathematician may never touch algebra.
entries.definitionCN: 主要指从事符号方程工作的人；数学家未必接触代数。

entries.definition: An older and more formal word for a worker in geometry, still used for classical studies of shape.
entries.definitionCN: 指几何工作者的更旧更正式的说法，仍用于对形的古典研究。

entries.definition: One who works with data and probability; the training overlaps but the daily work differs.
entries.definitionCN: 指处理数据与概率的人；训练有重叠，但日常工作不同。

entries.definition: One who calculates risk and premiums for insurers, using mathematics as a tool rather than as a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 指为保险机构计算风险与保费的人，把数学当工具而非研究对象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The word is the field's name plus a person suffix, so it means one who lives by the field.
normal.cn: 这个词是学科名加表人后缀，因此指靠这门学问谋生的人。

normal.en: The Greek root says 'learned', so the earliest bearers of the name were simply people of learning.
normal.cn: 希腊词根意为「有学问的」，因此最早带这个名号的人只是有学问者。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the roles: pure mathematician, applied mathematician, a team of mathematicians.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出角色：纯数学家、应用数学家、一组数学家。

normal.en: In Shakespeare's time the same word could mean an astrologer, since star-reading was then calculation.
normal.cn: 在莎士比亚时代，同一个词可指占星者，因为读星象当时属于计算。

normal.en: The family runs mathematics, mathematical, mathematician, mathematically, plus the old form mathematic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括数学、数学的、数学家、在数学上，另有旧形式「数学的」。

abstract.en: Picture a person who fills a wall with a single proof and then sleeps beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人把一整面墙写满同一个证明，然后就在旁边睡下。

abstract.en: Picture a locksmith who never touches a door but knows every lock in the city.
abstract.cn: 想象一位锁匠从不碰门，却熟悉全城每一把锁。

abstract.en: Picture a chess player who sees the board three moves before anyone else does.
abstract.cn: 想象一位棋手，比旁人早三步看见棋盘。

examples.en: The mathematician published the proof in a journal read by few.
examples.cn: 这位数学家把证明发表在一份读者很少的期刊上。

examples.en: Applied mathematicians now work closely with surgeons.
examples.cn: 应用数学家如今与外科医生密切合作。

examples.en: As a mathematician she distrusted any argument that skipped a step.
examples.cn: 作为数学家，她不信任任何跳过一步的论证。

dict_mnemonic.text: 记作「学数学的人」：学科名换上一个表人尾巴 → 数学家

root: 希腊 mathēma「所学之物」+ 拉丁 -ianus 表人后缀（经法语入英语）；拉丁 mathematicus 兼指数学研习者与占星者；十六、十七世纪英语中可指占星术士，十九世纪固定为现代数学家。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the researcher to the teacher, the number-skilled person, the branch specialist, the historical author, the old astrologer, the industrial modeller, and finally the calculating character of a negotiator.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从研究者，移到教师、擅长数字者、分支专家、历史著作者、旧时的占星者、工业建模者，最后到谈判者身上那种精于算计的气质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a desk with symbol-covered pages and a small board holding an unfinished proof.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张桌子，上面是写满符号的纸，旁边小黑板留着未完成的证明。

branches.en: Research and teaching: the same training spent either on new proofs or on other people's lessons.
branches.cn: 研究与教学：同样的训练，或用于新证明，或用于他人的课。

branches.en: Number sense, plain and figurative: a compliment at a till, a metaphor at a negotiating table.
branches.cn: 数字感，字面与比喻：收银台边的称赞，谈判桌上的隐喻。

branches.en: The narrow branch and the remembered book: expertise can be local or historical.
branches.cn: 窄分支与留存的书：专长可以是局部的，也可以是历史的。

branches.en: The old stars: the same name once covered those who read horoscopes.
branches.cn: 旧时的星：同一个名号曾涵盖读星盘的人。

branches.en: The market: the same skill sold as modelling for insurers and engineers.
branches.cn: 市场：同样的技能作为建模卖给保险与工程。

intro.en: The word is a Greek stem with a Greek adjective suffix, then a Latin person suffix, all of which also build the rest of the family.
intro.cn: 这个词是希腊词干加希腊形容词后缀，再加拉丁表人后缀，这些部件也构成词族其余部分。

latinIntro.en: Greek mathēma supplies 'learning', -ikos marks belonging, and Latin -ianus (through French) marks a person.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语名词提供「学习」之义，希腊后缀标记「属于」，拉丁后缀经法语标记人。

items.example: The stem supplies the learning at the heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干提供词心处的「学问」。

items.example: The suffix turns the noun into the adjective from which the person name is built.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成形容词，再由它构成表人之名。

items.example: The Greek adjective is the base of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊形容词是英语名词的基础。

items.example: The Latin suffix marks a person associated with the field.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁后缀标记与该领域有关的人。

items.example: The English ending is the everyday person marker for trades and fields.
items.exampleCN: 这个英语词尾是行业与领域的常用表人标记。

items.example: The word names the practitioner rather than the practice.
items.exampleCN: 这个词指从业者而非这门实践。

items.example: The field name is what the person name is built on.
items.exampleCN: 表人之名建立在学科名上。

items.example: The adjective describes the work rather than the worker.
items.exampleCN: 形容词描述工作而非工作者。

items.example: The adverb marks the manner of working.
items.exampleCN: 副词标记工作的方式。

latinEntries.structure: mathēma, mathēmatos (n., third declension, Greek loan)

definition_zh: 数学；数学学科；（某事物的）数学计算部分
definition_en: the branch of study that deals with numbers, quantities, shapes and the relations between them, using logical reasoning
core_image: 一整面黑板上密密的算式，粉笔灰落在槽沿，最后一行的等号被重重描了一遍
scene: 教室里一整面黑板写满算式，一名学生在角落补上一个等号，粉笔灰落在槽沿。She studied mathematics for four years before turning to economics.
sceneCN: 这里 mathematics 指「作为一门学科的数学」（第 1 个义项：研究数与形及其关系的学问）；句意为她学了四年数学之后才转向经济学。图中可辨识物件：黑板、粉笔、算式、板槽；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 数学（学科名，形式为复数而作单数用）

senses.title: The discipline as a whole
senses.definition: the field of study that reasons about number, quantity, structure and shape
senses.definitionCN: 研究数、量、结构与形的学问领域
senses.example: She studied mathematics for four years before turning to economics.
senses.exampleCN: 她学了四年数学之后才转向经济学。
senses.why: The word names a whole discipline rather than one of its branches, so it is used with a singular verb despite its plural shape.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是整门学问而非某一分支，因此尽管外形是复数，却接单数动词。

senses.title: The school subject and its lessons
senses.definition: the subject taught in schools, together with the lessons and examinations that go with it
senses.definitionCN: 学校里教授的这一科目，以及随之而来的课程与考试
senses.example: Mathematics is timetabled before lunch three days a week.
senses.exampleCN: 数学课每周有三天排在午饭前。
senses.why: Once a discipline enters a timetable it becomes a subject, and the same word covers both the field and the hour it occupies.
senses.whyCN: 一门学问一旦进入课表就成了科目，同一个词既指这个领域，也指它占用的那一节课。

senses.title: Reckoning and reasoning in practice
senses.titleCN: 实际推算与推理的活动
senses.definition: the activity of calculating and reasoning with numbers in a particular situation
senses.definitionCN: 在具体情境中运用数字进行计算与推理的活动
senses.example: The mathematics behind the bridge design was checked twice.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥设计背后的数学计算被核对了两遍。
senses.why: Here the word means the working itself, not the science of it: the sums someone actually did.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词指实际运算本身，而不是关于运算的学问：某人真做过的那些计算。

senses.title: The mathematical side of a subject
senses.titleCN: 某一对象内部的数学机制
senses.definition: the quantitative structure and relationships that underlie a particular process or system
senses.definitionCN: 支撑某一过程或系统的数量结构与关系
senses.example: The mathematics of traffic flow decides where queues form.
senses.exampleCN: 车流的数学机制决定了排队会在哪里形成。
senses.why: Any system with regular quantities has a mathematics of its own, and the phrase names that structure rather than the discipline.
senses.whyCN: 任何具有规律数量的系统都有自己的数学，这个说法指那套结构，而非那门学科。

senses.title: The professional community
senses.definition: the community of people who work in the field, taken as a body
senses.definitionCN: 以整体看待的、从事这一领域的人所组成的群体
senses.example: The result was celebrated across mathematics before it was published.
senses.exampleCN: 这一结果在发表之前就已在数学界传开。
senses.why: A discipline also names its practitioners as a group, which is why one can speak of a whole field being excited.
senses.whyCN: 一门学问也指其从业者的群体，因此可以说整个领域为之振奋。

senses.title: Careful reckoning in plain speech
senses.definition: used informally for the calculating needed to make a decision come out right
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指为使某项决定算得过来所需的精密推算
senses.example: The mathematics of the deal did not survive the new tax.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔交易的账在新税之下算不过来了。
senses.why: Everyday speech borrows the discipline's name for the arithmetic of a practical decision.
senses.whyCN: 日常说法借这门学问之名，指一项实际决定背后的加减账。

senses.title: The old sense of learning
senses.definition: in its Greek origin, any branch of learning rather than the numerical sciences alone
senses.definitionCN: 在其希腊来源中泛指任何一门学问，而非仅指数理科学
senses.example: In the ancient curriculum, music and astronomy counted as mathematics.
senses.exampleCN: 在古代课程里，音乐与天文也算作数学。
senses.why: The Greek word meant something learned, so the discipline once covered far more ground than it does now.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语原词意为「被学到的东西」，因此这门学问早先涵盖的范围远大于今天。

senses.title: The mathematical content of a paper
senses.titleCN: 论文或模型中的数学内容
senses.definition: the equations, proofs and derivations contained in a piece of work
senses.definitionCN: 一项工作中所含的方程、证明与推导
senses.example: The biology paper was strong, but its mathematics was thin.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇生物学论文很强，但其中的数学部分薄弱。
senses.why: Readers separate a work's subject matter from its mathematical machinery, and this sense names the latter.
senses.whyCN: 读者会把一项工作的主题与其数学工具分开，这个义项指后者。

intro.en: The word goes back to Greek mathēma 'that which is learned', from manthanein 'to learn'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词可追溯到希腊语 mathēma「被学到的东西」，源自动词 manthanein「学习」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Manthanein meant 'to learn', and gave mathēma 'a lesson, something learned' and mathesis 'learning'. The deeper root is reconstructed, not attested.
items.cn: manthanein 意为「学习」，由此得到 mathēma「课业、所学之物」与 mathesis「学习」。更深词根属重构形式，并无实证。

items.en: Mathēmatikos meant 'fond of learning, learned'; ta mathēmatika named the things studied rather than a single science.
items.cn: mathēmatikos 意为「爱学习的、有学问的」；中性复数形式指的是所学的那些东西，而非单一学科。

items.en: The phrase mathēmatikē tekhnē, 'the art of learning', was narrowed by Plato and Aristotle to arithmetic, geometry, astronomy and music.
items.cn: 「学习的技艺」这一短语经柏拉图与亚里士多德之手，收窄为算术、几何、天文与音乐四门。

items.en: Latin took mathematica as a name for that group of studies, and medieval schools taught them in the quadrivial curriculum.
items.cn: 拉丁语以 mathematica 作为这组学问之名，中世纪学校在四艺课程中教授它们。

items.en: English adopted the word in the sixteenth century; the plural form is treated as singular because it names one field.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪吸收这个词；复数外形被当作单数使用，因为它命名的是一个领域。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the field expanded far beyond number and shape, and the old sense of any learning survives only in histories of the curriculum. First date uncertain: the earliest English citation is placed in the sixteenth century but no single year is agreed.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，该领域远远超出数与形，而「任何学问」的旧义只留在课程史中。首见年代不确定：最早英语书证被放在十六世纪，但没有公认的确切年份。

note.en: Group one separates forms of the same word that are easy to mix up; group two separates the neighbouring branches of the field.
note.cn: 第一组辨析同一个词的各种形式，第二组辨析相邻的学科分支。

entries.definition: An older singular and adjective form, now rare; modern English keeps the plural shape for the field and uses mathematical for the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 更早的单数形式与形容词形式，今已罕用；现代英语以复数外形指该领域，形容词则另用形式。

entries.definition: The adjective of the field; it describes work or reasoning rather than naming the discipline itself.
entries.definitionCN: 该领域的形容词；它描述工作或推理，而不命名学科本身。

entries.definition: The practitioner; the ending marks a person, which is the one clear difference from the field name.
entries.definitionCN: 指从业者；词尾标记出人，这是与学科名唯一清楚的差别。

entries.definition: A rare English borrowing of the Greek noun for learning, used in older philosophical writing; it never named the school subject.
entries.definitionCN: 英语直接从希腊语借入的罕见名词，意为学习，见于较早的哲学写作；它从未指学校科目。

entries.definition: The branch that handles counting and the four operations; it is a part of mathematics, not a synonym for it.
entries.definitionCN: 处理计数与四则运算的分支；它是数学的一部分，而不是数学的同义词。

entries.definition: The branch that works with symbols standing for unknown numbers; one department within the larger field.
entries.definitionCN: 用符号代表未知数进行运算的分支；是更大领域中的一个部门。

entries.definition: The branch that studies shape, size and the relations of figures in space.
entries.definitionCN: 研究形状、大小与空间中图形关系的分支。

entries.definition: The practical ability to handle numbers in daily life; it is a skill, whereas mathematics is a discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 在日常生活中处理数字的实际能力；它是一种技能，而数学是一门学问。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Greek root means 'that which is learned', so mathematics began as the name for any studied subject.
normal.cn: 希腊词根意为「被学到的东西」，因此数学最初泛指任何被研习的科目。

normal.en: The plural shape takes a singular verb: mathematics is one field, not many.
normal.cn: 复数外形接单数动词：数学是一个领域，而不是许多个。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the division of the field: pure mathematics, applied mathematics, advanced mathematics.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域的划分：纯数学、应用数学、高等数学。

normal.en: The family runs mathematics, mathematical, mathematician, mathematically, plus the clippings math and maths.
normal.cn: 同族词包括数学、数学的、数学家、在数学上，另有口语缩略形式。

normal.en: Ancient schooling grouped it with music and astronomy, so the old sense was wider than today's.
normal.cn: 古代课程把它与音乐、天文编在一起，因此旧义比今天宽。

abstract.en: Picture a single chalk line drawn again and again until it is unmistakably straight.
abstract.cn: 想象一条粉笔线被反复描画，直到直得无可置疑。

abstract.en: Picture a key ring that opens every locked door in a building, whatever the door was made for.
abstract.cn: 想象一串钥匙能打开楼里每一扇锁着的门，无论那扇门原本是做什么用的。

abstract.en: Picture a language spoken by few people but understood, in translation, by everyone.
abstract.cn: 想象一种只有少数人会说的语言，却人人能通过翻译读懂。

examples.en: Mathematics is compulsory for every student in the first two years.
examples.cn: 头两年每个学生都必须学数学。

examples.en: The mathematics of the model turned out to be simpler than expected.
examples.cn: 这个模型的数学部分比预想的简单。

examples.en: He teaches mathematics at a secondary school.
examples.cn: 他在一所中学教数学。

dict_mnemonic.text: 记作「学来的东西」：希腊词根意为学习，凡学得的学问都算 → 数学

root: 希腊 mathēma「被学到的东西」源自动词 manthanein「学习」，mathēmatikē tekhnē 经柏拉图与亚里士多德收窄为四艺；拉丁 mathematica 承之，英语十六世纪借入，复数外形作单数用。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the discipline as a whole to its school hours, its practical working, the structure inside another subject, its professional community, plain-speech reckoning, the ancient sense of any learning, and the mathematics inside a single paper.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从作为整体的学科，移到它的课时、实际运算、另一对象内部的结构、专业共同体、口语里的算账、古代泛指学问的旧义，最后到一篇论文里的数学部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blackboard filled with lines of symbols, one equal sign pressed hard at the end.
core.cn: 核心意象：写满符号行的黑板，末尾一个被重重描过的等号。

branches.en: The field and its old name: what began as any studied subject became one discipline.
branches.cn: 领域与其旧名：最初泛指任何被研习的科目，后来成了一口学科。

branches.en: Where it is taught and where it is printed: a timetable hour and a thin section of a paper.
branches.cn: 教它的地方与印它的地方：课表上的一节，论文里薄弱的一节。

branches.en: Reckoning in practice: the sums behind a bridge or behind a deal.
branches.cn: 实际算账：桥背后的算式，或一笔交易背后的账。

branches.en: The hidden structure: every regular system carries a mathematics of its own.
branches.cn: 隐在的结构：每个有规律的系统都自带一套数学。

branches.en: The people: a field is also the body of those who work in it.
branches.cn: 人：一个领域也是从事者的群体。

intro.en: The English word is a Greek noun with a Greek suffix, filtered through Latin and given an English plural ending.
intro.cn: 这个英语词是一个希腊名词加希腊后缀，经拉丁语过滤，又换上英语复数词尾。

latinIntro.en: Greek mathēma and mathēmatikos supply the meaning; Latin mathematica fixed the school subject, and English added the plural -s.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语的名词与形容词提供意义；拉丁语固定了学科之名，英语再加复数词尾。

items.example: The root names learning before it names number.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根先指学习，后指数。

items.example: The verb stands at the head of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词位于整个词族的起点。

items.example: The suffix names a skilled practice, not a body of facts.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名一门技艺，而非一堆事实。

items.meaningCN: 有学问的；属于数学之物的
items.example: The adjective shifted from 'learned' to 'numerical'.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词从「有学问的」转为「数理的」。

items.example: Latin fixed the plural shape that English inherited.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语固定了英语所继承的复数外形。

items.structure: English plural ending used for fields of study
items.example: The ending marks a discipline while keeping a plural look.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记一门学科，同时保留复数外形。

items.example: The word names one field with a plural form.
items.exampleCN: 这个词以复数形式命名一个领域。

items.example: The adjective serves whenever a noun follows.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词用于修饰后面的名词。

items.meaning: a person who works in the field
items.example: The person suffix completes the family.
items.exampleCN: 表人后缀补全了词族。

latinEntries.structure: mathesis, mathesis (f., third declension, from Greek)

definition_zh: 物质；事情；问题；要紧、有关系；【医】脓液
definition_en: the physical stuff that things are made of, an affair under discussion, or to be important
core_image: 一块被雨水泡软的黑泥，手指一捏就能变形，也能弄脏任何碰到它的东西
scene: 泥地刚被雨水浸透，脚一踩就陷下去，鞋底带起黏稠的一团。The sticky mud is the matter that stains every boot in the yard.
sceneCN: 这里 matter 指构成物体的有形之物（第 1 个义项：与形式相对、可被感官触及的实体材料）；句意：那团黏泥就是弄脏院子里每只靴子的物质。图中可辨识物件：泥洼、沾泥的靴子、铁锹、水桶；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 物质；事情；问题；脓液
要紧；有重大关系

forms.label: 单数（物质义通常不可数）

derivatives.zh: 就事论事的；不动声色的（由本词与「事实」一词构成的复合形容词）
反物质（加表示「相反」的前缀构成，指电荷相反的物质）
无实质内容的（加表示「没有」的后缀构成）
含脓的（加形容词后缀构成，旧医学用法，现已罕用）

senses.title: Physical substance
senses.definition: the physical substance that occupies space and can be seen or touched
senses.definitionCN: 占据空间、可被看见或摸到的实体材料
senses.example: The sticky mud is the matter that stains every boot in the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 那团黏泥就是弄脏院子里每只靴子的物质。
senses.why: matter goes back to Latin materia, which meant timber and the stuff a thing is built from, so the physical sense is the oldest layer.
senses.whyCN: matter 上溯到拉丁 materia，本指木料与造物所用的料，因此「有形之物」是最古老的一层意思。

senses.title: An affair or business
senses.titleCN: 一件待办或已办的事情
senses.definition: a situation, event or piece of business that someone deals with
senses.definitionCN: 某人需要处理的情境、事件或事务
senses.example: She settled a few private matters before leaving for the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 去海边之前，她先处理了几件私事。
senses.why: Latin materia also named the subject under discussion, so the stuff of a talk became the affair itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 materia 也指谈论的题目，于是「谈话的料」就变成了「事情本身」。

senses.title: A problem to be solved
senses.titleCN: 出了差错、需要弄清的问题
senses.definition: a trouble or difficulty, especially one whose cause is not yet known
senses.definitionCN: 麻烦或困难，尤指原因尚未查明的那一种
senses.example: The mechanic asked what the matter was with the engine.
senses.exampleCN: 修理工问发动机出了什么毛病。
senses.why: an affair that has gone wrong is still an affair, so the same word shifted from business to trouble.
senses.whyCN: 出了岔子的事情仍然是一件事情，这个词便从「事务」滑到「麻烦」。

senses.title: To be important
senses.definition: to be of importance or consequence to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某事具有重要性或后果
senses.example: Accuracy matters more than speed in this laboratory.
senses.exampleCN: 在这间实验室里，准确比速度更要紧。
senses.why: what has substance has weight, and English turned that picture into the verb sense of counting for something.
senses.whyCN: 有实体就有分量，英语把这个画面变成了「算得上数」的动词义。

senses.title: The topic of a text or talk
senses.definition: the subject or content that a piece of writing, speech or study is about
senses.definitionCN: 一篇文章、一段讲话或一项研究所谈论的主题与内容
senses.example: The matter of the lecture was soil chemistry in dry regions.
senses.exampleCN: 那场讲座的主题是干旱地区的土壤化学。
senses.why: the material of a text is what it carries, and that carrying sense became the topic it treats.
senses.whyCN: 文章的「料」就是它所承载的东西，这一承载义再转为它所处理的主题。

senses.title: Grounds for concern
senses.titleCN: 值得忧虑或申诉的根据
senses.definition: a reason or grounds for a feeling, claim or action
senses.definitionCN: 某种情绪、主张或行动的根据与理由
senses.example: The inspectors found matter for concern in the water samples.
senses.exampleCN: 检查人员在采水样中发现了值得忧虑的情况。
senses.why: a matter is something that exists and can be pointed at, so it came to mean a fact solid enough to base a claim on.
senses.whyCN: 事情是存在且指得出的事物，于是引申为「站得住脚、可作依据的事实」。

senses.title: Pus from a wound
senses.definition: the fluid that forms in an infected wound, formerly called matter
senses.definitionCN: 感染伤口中生成的液体，旧时称作 matter
senses.example: The old surgical notes describe the wound discharging matter.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的手术记录描述伤口流出脓液。
senses.why: early medicine used matter for any fluid substance of the body, and pus was simply the matter a wound produced.
senses.whyCN: 早期医学用 matter 泛指体内各种液体，脓不过是伤口生成的「物质」。

senses.title: Content as opposed to form
senses.titleCN: 与形式相对的实质内容
senses.definition: the substantive content of a work, as distinct from its style or outward form
senses.definitionCN: 作品的实际内容，与风格或外在形式相对
senses.example: The matter of the essay outweighs its elegant phrasing.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇随笔的内容比它漂亮的措辞更有分量。
senses.why: philosophy opposed matter to form, and literary criticism then asked whether a work had matter behind its shape.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把「质料」与「形式」对举，文学批评随后追问一部作品在形之外有没有实质。

intro.en: Matter came into English through Old French from Latin materia 'timber, stuff, subject'. The common claim that materia derives from mater 'mother' is a hypothesis, not a settled derivation.
intro.cn: matter 经古法语来自拉丁 materia「木料、材料、题目」。常有人说 materia 由 mater「母亲」派生，那是假说，并非已定的词源。

items.en: Materia meant timber and the material a thing is made from, and by extension the subject of a discussion.
items.cn: materia 指木料以及造物所用的材料，引申为谈论的题目。

items.en: A widely repeated suggestion links materia to mater 'mother', as if the stuff were the mother of the object; this remains a hypothesis and is not established.
items.cn: 一种广为流传的说法把 materia 与 mater「母亲」联系起来，仿佛材料是器物的母亲；这仍属假说，未获证实。

items.en: Old French matere carried both the physical sense and the sense of a subject or affair into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 matere 在诺曼时期之后把「物质」与「题目、事务」两义一并带入英语。

items.en: Middle English matter already covered stuff, a business, a question and grounds for complaint, so the wide sense range is old, not modern.
items.cn: 中古英语的 matter 已兼指物质、事务、问题与申诉的理由，可见义域之宽古已有之，并非现代才有。

items.en: Medical writing of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries used matter for bodily fluid and especially for pus, a use that has since narrowed.
items.cn: 十六、十七世纪的医学文献用 matter 指体液，尤指脓，这一用法后来收窄。

items.en: The first recorded dates for several senses are approximate; the word itself is well attested from the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 若干义项的最早记录年代为约数；这个词本身在十三世纪已有充分书证。

note.en: The first group contains forms that look or sound close to matter but may sit on a different root; the second group contains words that share part of its meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是形或音与 matter 接近、但未必同源的词；第二组是与之部分同义的词。

entries.definition: Built on Latin materialis from materia, so it is the adjective and noun grown from the same stock as matter, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 由拉丁 materialis 构成，而 materialis 出自 materia，因此它是与 matter 同出一源的名词与形容词，并非另一个词根。

entries.definition: A French-shaped doublet of material, borrowed later for military equipment and supplies; it shares the Latin source but not the everyday meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 是 material 的法语式借形词，后借入指军用装备与物资；与 material 同源，但日常义不同。

entries.definition: From Latin mater 'mother' through maternellus; it is related to mater, and only through the unproven mater-materia hypothesis could it be called a cousin of matter.
entries.definitionCN: 经 maternellus 出自拉丁 mater「母亲」；它与 mater 有关，只有借助尚未证实的「母亲—材料」假说，才能算作 matter 的远亲。

entries.definition: From Latin matrix 'womb, mould', built on mater; it names a mould or grid, and does not descend from materia.
entries.definitionCN: 出自拉丁 matrix「子宫、模具」，由 mater 构成；它指模具或网格，并非由 materia 传下。

entries.definition: Physical stuff considered as what stands under qualities; matter stresses the material, substance stresses independent existence.
entries.definitionCN: 把物质看作承载属性的基底；matter 强调材料，substance 强调独立存在。

entries.definition: A matter of business or public concern; it covers only the affair sense and never the physical one.
entries.definitionCN: 指事务或公众关注之事；只覆盖「事务」义，绝不指物质。

entries.definition: A topic on which people disagree; it is narrower than matter because it always implies debate.
entries.definitionCN: 指人们有分歧的议题；比 matter 窄，因为它总含争辩之意。

entries.definition: The everyday word for unspecified material; matter is its neutral and technical counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指未指明材料的日常说法；matter 是它中性、技术化的对应词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin source, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁来源、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin materia first meant timber, so matter is the stuff a thing is built from.
normal.cn: 拉丁 materia 最初指木料，因此 matter 就是造物所用的料。

normal.en: The family runs matter, material, materially, immaterial and materialize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 matter、material、materially、immaterial 与 materialize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the affair sense: a matter of time, as a matter of fact, no matter what.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出「事情」义：只是时间问题、事实上、无论发生什么。

normal.en: Subject matter keeps the topic sense visible in publishing and teaching.
normal.cn: 「主题素材」这一说法让「主题」义在出版与教学里一直可见。

normal.en: The verb is used in questions of value: it matters, it does not matter.
normal.cn: 动词义出现在价值判断里：这要紧、这不要紧。

abstract.en: Picture a lump of clay that takes the shape of whatever presses into it.
abstract.cn: 想象一团黏土，什么按上去就留下什么形状。

abstract.en: Picture a desk with one folded note on it, and everyone asks about that note first.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上只有一张折起的字条，所有人先问的都是那张字条。

abstract.en: Picture a scale where the pan with real goods sinks and the empty pan rises.
abstract.cn: 想象一杆秤，装了实物的那端沉下去，空的那端翘起来。

examples.en: In legal drafting, the matter of a contract means its operative content rather than its layout.
examples.cn: 在法律起草中，合同的 matter 指其有效内容，而不是排版。

examples.en: Dark matter does not emit light, yet its gravity holds galaxies together.
examples.cn: 暗物质不发光，但它的引力把星系维系在一起。

examples.en: It does not matter how slowly you go as long as the measurements stay exact.
examples.cn: 只要测量保持精确，你走得多慢都不要紧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「妈特」——妈妈特别在意的那件事，就是要紧的事 → 事情、要紧；妈妈捏的那团泥，就是物质

root: 拉丁 materia「木料、材料、题目」（一说由 mater「母亲」派生，仅为常见假说）→ 古法语 matere「材料、事务」→ 英语 matter；「问题」与「脓」义由「事情」「体内物质」再引申。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses radiate from one lump of stuff: it is the material of things, then the material of talk, then the affair, the trouble inside it, the fact that carries weight, the topic of a text, the fluid in a wound, and finally content set against form.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一团「料」辐射出去：先是造物的材料，再是谈话的材料，继而成为事情、事情里的麻烦、有分量的事实、文本的主题、伤口的液体，最后是与形式相对的实质内容。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lump of wet clay that can be shaped, weighed and pointed at.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团湿黏土，可被塑形、称重、指认。

branches.en: THE LUMP ITSELF: clay in the yard and pus in a wound are both stuff a body or a boot meets.
branches.cn: 这团东西本身：院里的泥与伤口的脓，都是身体或靴子会碰到的实体。

branches.en: THE AFFAIR AND ITS SNAG: business first, then the trouble discovered inside it.
branches.cn: 事情与其中的疙瘩：先是事务，再是事务里查出的麻烦。

branches.en: WEIGHT THAT COUNTS: what has substance can tip a decision, so matter becomes a verb.
branches.cn: 有分量才算数：有实体就能压动决定，于是 matter 变成动词。

branches.en: STUFF POINTED AT: the material of a text turns into its topic, and a solid fact into grounds.
branches.cn: 被指认的料：文本的材料变成主题，扎实的事实变成依据。

branches.en: CONTENT AGAINST FORM: philosophy keeps the lump as what remains when style is stripped away.
branches.cn: 内容对形式：哲学把那团料保留为剥去风格后剩下的东西。

intro.en: Matter is built on a Latin root that also yields material and immaterial, so the family can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: matter 建立在一个拉丁词根上，同一词根还生出 material 与 immaterial，因此这个词族可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin materia supplies matter, material and materialis; mater supplies maternal and matrix, with the materia link remaining a hypothesis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 materia 衍生 matter 与 material 一系；mater 衍生 maternal 与 matrix 一系，而 materia 与 mater 的联系仍属假说。

items.example: The root gives the picture of stuff a thing is built from.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根给出「造物所用之料」的画面。

items.example: Its link to materia is a hypothesis, not a proven derivation.
items.exampleCN: 它与 materia 的联系只是假说，并非已证的派生。

items.example: The adjective suffix turns stuff into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 形容词后缀把「料」变成描述性的词。

items.example: Material keeps both the physical and the serious sense.
items.exampleCN: material 兼有「物质」与「重要」两义。

items.example: It also shapes editorial and commercial.
items.exampleCN: 它同样构成 editorial 与 commercial。

items.example: The negation covers both the physical and the serious sense.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀同时否掉「物质」与「重要」两义。

items.example: The plan materialized as a real building.
items.exampleCN: 计划落实成了一座真实的建筑。

items.example: The later borrowing narrowed to army supplies.
items.exampleCN: 后借入的这一形收窄为军队物资。

definition_zh: 成熟的；成年的；深思熟虑的；使成熟；成熟；到期
definition_en: fully grown or fully developed, especially in fruit, wine, or a person; showing adult judgment; as a verb, to become fully developed or to reach the date when a financial product must be paid
core_image: 枝头的果子由青转红：酸涩退去，甜味与重量一起到位，才到了可以摘下的那一刻
scene: 果园里，农人捏了捏枝头的桃子。The peach gave slightly under his thumb, and only when it was mature did he cut it down and put it in the basket.
sceneCN: 这里 mature 是「果实成熟」（第 1 个义项：水果、作物达到可食用的成熟状态）；句意：桃子在他拇指下微微软了，只有确认它成熟了，他才摘下来放进筐里。图中可辨识物件：桃树枝、成熟的桃子、农人的手、果筐；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 成熟的；成年的；深思熟虑的；到期的
使成熟；成熟；到期

senses.title: Fruit or wine: ripe and ready
senses.titleCN: 果实或酒：熟到可以用了
senses.definition: of fruit, grain, or wine, fully ripened and ready to be eaten, harvested, or drunk
senses.definitionCN: 指水果、谷物或酒已完全成熟，可以食用、收割或饮用
senses.example: The peaches are mature enough to pick today.
senses.exampleCN: 这些桃子今天已经熟到可以摘了。
senses.why: The adjective is first recorded in the mid-15c. of fruits, meaning 'ripe, complete in natural growth or development'. The image is biological: growth has finished, and the fruit has reached the point it was growing toward.
senses.whyCN: 形容词义在 15 世纪中期首次记录，用于水果，意为“成熟的、在自然生长或发育上已完成的”。画面是生物性的：生长已经结束，果实到达了它一直生长所要到达的那一点。

senses.title: A person fully grown in body and mind
senses.definition: of a person, having fully developed powers of body and mind; adult
senses.definitionCN: 指人在身体与心智能力上已充分发育；成年的
senses.example: The study compares mature adults with teenagers.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究把成年人与青少年作比较。
senses.why: Of persons, the sense 'having fully developed powers of body and mind' is recorded c. 1600. The biological image is transferred from fruit to people: development has reached its intended end, though growth in learning may continue.
senses.whyCN: 用于人时，“身体与心智能力已充分发育”的义项记录于约 1600 年。生物意象从果实移到了人：发育已达到预定的终点，尽管学识上的成长仍可继续。

senses.title: Adult judgment: behaving with maturity
senses.titleCN: 成年人的判断力：表现得成熟
senses.definition: showing the emotional calm and responsibility expected of an adult, especially in a difficult situation
senses.definitionCN: 在困难处境中表现出成年人应有的情绪稳定与责任感
senses.example: She gave a mature answer instead of blaming someone else.
senses.exampleCN: 她没有责怪别人，而是给出了一个成熟的回答。
senses.why: This is the evaluative branch: mature no longer describes the body but the response. The word praises someone for having reached the emotional end-point that adulthood is supposed to bring.
senses.whyCN: 这是评价性的分支：mature 描述的不再是身体，而是反应方式。这个词在称赞一个人达到了成年本应带来的情绪终点。

senses.title: A well-considered plan or judgment
senses.titleCN: 经过充分考虑的计划或判断
senses.definition: of a plan, idea, or judgment, careful, thorough, and reached after long thought
senses.definitionCN: 指计划、想法或判断审慎、周全，并经过长时间思考才形成
senses.example: After months of review, they submitted a mature proposal.
senses.exampleCN: 经过数月审议，他们提交了一份成熟的方案。
senses.why: The same mid-15c. entry that named ripe fruit also named 'careful, well-considered, thorough' deliberations. An idea, like fruit, needs time before it is ready; rushing it gives a green, sour result.
senses.whyCN: 15 世纪中期记录“成熟果实”的同一条目，也记录了“审慎、周全、彻底”的思考。一个想法和果实一样，需要时间才能就绪；催熟只会得到青涩的结果。

senses.title: To ripen: make or become mature
senses.definition: to bring something to full ripeness, or to come to a state of ripeness
senses.definitionCN: 使某物完全成熟，或进入成熟状态
senses.example: The cheese is left to mature for eighteen months.
senses.exampleCN: 这种奶酪要放置十八个月让它成熟。
senses.why: The verb appears c. 1400 as 'encourage suppuration', then in the mid-15c. as 'cause to ripen'. The intransitive sense 'become ripe' is from the 1650s. The medical origin is literal: a swelling also comes to a head in its own time.
senses.whyCN: 动词义约在 1400 年出现，意为“促使化脓”，15 世纪中期转为“使成熟”。“自己变得成熟”的不及物义来自 17 世纪 50 年代。医学来源是字面的：肿胀也会在自己的时间里“长熟”。

senses.title: A market, product, or artist developing fully
senses.titleCN: 市场、产品或艺术家发展至完善
senses.definition: of an industry, product, style, or career, to develop over time into a settled and fully formed state
senses.definitionCN: 指行业、产品、风格或事业随时间发展，进入稳定而完整的状态
senses.example: The market matured quickly once the standards were agreed.
senses.exampleCN: 标准一旦达成一致，这个市场很快就成熟了。
senses.why: Growth in business follows the same curve as growth in a plant: an early unstable phase, then a settled phase. Calling a market mature means it has stopped expanding wildly and has found its shape.
senses.whyCN: 商业上的成长与植物的成长走同一条曲线：先是早期不稳定阶段，然后是稳定阶段。说一个市场 mature，意味着它已停止疯狂扩张，找到了自己的形状。

senses.title: Finance: reach the date of payment
senses.definition: of a bond, policy, or loan, to reach the date on which the principal must be paid
senses.definitionCN: 指债券、保单或贷款到达必须偿付本金的日期
senses.example: The bond matures in ten years, but the interest is paid twice a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这只债券十年后到期，但利息每年支付两次。
senses.why: The financial sense 'reach the time for payment' is recorded by 1861. A debt, like fruit, has a fixed season: it is not paid early, but at the point when it has become 'due', from Latin maturus 'timely'.
senses.whyCN: 金融义“到达付款时间”记录于 1861 年。债务和果实一样有固定的季节：不提前偿付，而是在它“到期”的那一点——maturus 本义就是“及时的”。

senses.title: A polite word for older
senses.titleCN: 对“年纪较大”的委婉说法
senses.definition: used as a polite or euphemistic adjective for someone older than the usual age for a role
senses.definitionCN: 用作礼貌或委婉的形容词，指比某角色的通常年龄更大
senses.example: She returned to university as a mature student at forty.
senses.exampleCN: 她四十岁时以成年学生的身份重返大学。
senses.why: The euphemistic sense 'older than usual' is recorded by 1953. Instead of saying old, English says mature, borrowing the positive idea of full development to avoid the negative idea of decline.
senses.whyCN: “比通常年龄更大”的委婉义记录于 1953 年。英语不说 old，而说 mature，借“充分发展”的正面含义，避开“衰退”的负面含义。

senses.title: Usage boundary: mature, ripe, adult, old
senses.definition: mature is broader than ripe and more evaluative than adult; it describes full development, not age itself, so it is not a neutral synonym of old
senses.definitionCN: mature 比 ripe 更宽，比 adult 更具评价性；它描述充分发展，而不是年龄本身，因此不是 old 的中性同义词
senses.example: A mature person may be young; a ripe fruit is simply ready to eat.
senses.exampleCN: 成熟的人可能很年轻；熟透的果子只是到了能吃的时候。
senses.why: Ripe belongs to fruit and grain; adult belongs to legal or biological age; mature adds judgment, readiness, and the completion of a process. The euphemistic use for age shows how easily the positive sense can be borrowed for a different purpose.
senses.whyCN: ripe 属于果实与谷物；adult 属于法定或生理年龄；mature 再加上判断力、就绪状态与过程的完成。用它对年龄作委婉表达，正说明这个正面义项多么容易被借去服务另一个目的。

intro.en: Mature comes from Latin maturus 'ripe, timely, early'. The word describes a process that has reached its proper point, and English extended it from fruit to people, plans, markets and debts. The deeper origin of maturus is not established.
intro.cn: mature 来自拉丁语 maturus“成熟的、及时的、早的”。这个词描述一个过程到达了它应有的节点，英语把它从果实扩展到人、计划、市场与债务。maturus 更深层的来源并未确立。

items.en: The verb is first recorded as maturen, 'encourage suppuration', then in the mid-15c. as 'cause to ripen, bring to maturity'. The earliest use is medical and agricultural, not moral.
items.cn: 动词最初记录为 maturen“促使化脓”，15 世纪中期转为“使成熟、带到成熟状态”。最早的用法是医学与农业的，而不是道德评价的。

items.en: The adjective appears of fruits, 'ripe, complete in natural growth or development', and of deliberations, 'careful, well-considered, thorough'.
items.cn: 形容词义出现，用于水果时意为“成熟的、自然生长或发育已完成的”，用于思考时意为“审慎的、周全的、彻底的”。

items.en: From Latin maturus 'ripe, timely, early', also the source of maturare 'to ripen, bring to maturity'. The link with mane 'early, of the morning' is standard.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 maturus“成熟的、及时的、早的”，也是 maturare“使成熟、带到成熟状态”的来源。它与 mane“早、清晨”的联系是通行说法。

items.en: The deeper origin of maturus is source uncertain. Some references cautiously connect it with a notion of 'ripeness' or with Latin manus 'good'; these are proposals, not established derivations, so no confident PIE root should be asserted.
items.cn: maturus 更深层的来源不确定。一些资料谨慎地把它与“成熟”的观念或拉丁语 manus“好”相联系；这些只是推测，不是已确立的派生关系，因此不应断言某个确定的原始印欧语词根。

items.en: Of persons, 'having fully developed powers of body and mind' is recorded c. 1600. The intransitive sense 'become ripe' follows in the 1650s.
items.cn: 用于人时，“身体与心智能力已充分发育”记录于约 1600 年。不及物义“变得成熟”随后在 17 世纪 50 年代出现。

items.en: The financial sense 'reach the time for payment' is recorded by 1861; the euphemistic sense 'older than usual' by 1953.
items.cn: 金融义“到达付款时间”记录于 1861 年；“比通常年龄更大”的委婉义记录于 1953 年。

note.en: The first group shares the maturus stem and its prefixes. The second group separates ripeness, legal adulthood, everyday grown-up behaviour and the softening that comes with age.
note.cn: 第一组共享 maturus 词干及其前缀。第二组区分果实成熟、法定成年、日常的“大人样”，以及随年龄而来的柔和。

entries.definition: the state of being mature, or the date when a financial product must be paid. It is the noun from mature.
entries.definitionCN: 成熟状态，或金融产品的到期日。它是 mature 的名词。

entries.definition: not fully developed, or behaving below the expected adult level. It adds the negative prefix in- to maturus.
entries.definitionCN: 未充分发育的，或行为低于成年人应有水平的。它在 maturus 前加了否定前缀 in-。

entries.definition: happening before the proper or expected time, as in a premature birth or a premature conclusion.
entries.definitionCN: 在应有或预期时间之前发生的，如早产或过早的结论。

entries.definition: ready to be eaten or harvested, especially of fruit or grain. It is narrower and more physical than mature.
entries.definitionCN: 可以食用或收割的，尤指水果或谷物。它比 mature 更窄、更具体。

entries.definition: fully grown or legally of age. It marks a stage of life, while mature also judges behaviour and judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 发育完全或达到法定年龄。它标记人生阶段，而 mature 还评价行为与判断力。

entries.definition: adult, or behaving in an adult way. It is more conversational and less evaluative than mature.
entries.definitionCN: 成年的，或表现得像大人。它比 mature 更口语化，评价性更弱。

entries.definition: softened and pleasant with age, as of wine, sound, or a person. It stresses gentleness, while mature stresses completion.
entries.definitionCN: 随年龄变得柔和、悦人，如酒、声音或人。它强调温和，而 mature 强调完成。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: maturus 'ripe, timely' gives mature, maturity, maturation, premature and immature; mane 'early' gives matins and matutinal.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实同族词：maturus“成熟的、及时的”给出 mature、maturity、maturation、premature、immature；mane“早”给出 matins、matutinal。

normal.en: Mature is a process word: something has reached the point it was growing toward. Fruit, wine, a person, a plan, a market and a bond can all arrive there.
normal.cn: mature 是一个过程词：某物到达了它一直生长所要到达的那一点。果实、酒、人、计划、市场、债券都可以到达那里。

normal.en: maturus means 'ripe' and also 'timely'. A mature bond is not old; it has simply reached its proper time.
normal.cn: maturus 既指“成熟”，也指“及时”。到期的债券不是“老”，它只是到达了它该到的时间。

normal.en: The verb first meant 'encourage suppuration' c. 1400: even an abscess was thought to come to a head in its own time. Ripening is a natural clock, not a push.
normal.cn: 动词约在 1400 年最早表示“促使化脓”：连脓肿也被认为会在自己的时间里“长熟”。成熟是一只自然的钟，不是硬推。

normal.en: The euphemism mature student (1953) borrows the positive sense of full development to avoid the word old.
normal.cn: mature student（1953）这个委婉说法，借“充分发展”的正面含义来避开 old 这个词。

normal.en: immature and premature are mature with a negative or a 'before' prefix: not yet developed, or developed too soon.
normal.cn: immature 与 premature 是给 mature 加上否定或“之前”的前缀：尚未发展，或发展得太早。

abstract.en: Picture a clock with no hands: you cannot see the time, only whether the fruit is still hard or finally soft. Mature is the moment the process says 'now'.
abstract.cn: 想象一只没有指针的钟：你看不见时间，只能看见果子还是硬的、或终于软了。mature 就是过程说出“现在”的那一刻。

abstract.en: The same curve runs through a peach, a wine, a mind, a manuscript, an industry and a debt: slow completion, then readiness.
abstract.cn: 同一条曲线穿过桃子、酒、心智、手稿、产业与债务：缓慢完成，然后就绪。

abstract.en: What is mature is not old; it is finished enough to be used. Old age is only one of the places where that readiness can be seen.
abstract.cn: 成熟的东西不是“老”，而是“完成到可以使用”。年老只是这种就绪状态可能被看见的场所之一。

examples.en: The wine needs another five years to mature properly.
examples.cn: 这酒还需要再放五年才能好好成熟。

examples.en: He handled the criticism in a mature way.
examples.cn: 他以成熟的方式对待批评。

examples.en: The loan matures at the end of March.
examples.cn: 这笔贷款在三月底到期。

dict_mnemonic.text: “马球”——马球运动员等到果子熟了才开赛，说这是成熟的决定 → mature 成熟的

root: 拉丁语 maturus“成熟的、及时的”，核心是“过程走到应有的节点、可以用了”，更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of mature, one ripening curve: ripe fruit, a grown person, adult judgment, a considered plan, the act of ripening, a settled market, a due debt, a polite word for older, and the boundary against ripe and old.
sensesIntro.cn: mature 的九个义项都是同一条成熟曲线：熟果、发育完全的人、成年人的判断、深思熟虑的计划、成熟的动作、稳定的市场、到期的债务、对年长的委婉说法，以及它与 ripe、old 的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a process reaches its proper point, and what has grown is now ready.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个过程到达了应有的节点，长成的东西现在可以用了。

branches.en: FRUIT AND WINE: biological ripening is the literal source of the whole family.
branches.cn: 果实与酒：生物性的成熟是整个词族最字面的来源。

branches.en: PERSON: the body finishes growing, and behaviour is expected to finish growing too.
branches.cn: 人：身体完成生长，行为也被期待完成“长大”。

branches.en: PROCESS: a plan and a market both need time before they are ready to be used.
branches.cn: 过程：计划与市场都需要时间，才能就绪可用。

branches.en: FINANCE: a debt has a season, and maturing is reaching that date.
branches.cn: 金融：债务有它的季节，到期就是走到那个日期。

branches.en: EUPHEMISM AND BOUNDARY: age is softened by the positive sense, and mature never simply means old.
branches.cn: 委婉与边界：年龄被正面义项柔化，而 mature 从不简单等于 old。

intro.en: Mature takes Latin prefixes and English suffixes: im- and pre- negate or shift time, while -ity, -ly and -ation build nouns and adverbs. The stem matur- stays constant.
intro.cn: mature 接受拉丁前缀与英语后缀：im- 与 pre- 表示否定或时间偏移，-ity、-ly、-ation 构成名词与副词。词干 matur- 保持不变。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family joins maturus 'ripe, timely' with mane 'early, morning': matins and matutinal belong to the morning, while premature means ripening before its time.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族把 maturus“成熟的、及时的”与 mane“早、清晨”连在一起：matins 与 matutinal 属于清晨，premature 则指在时间之前就成熟。

items.meaning: the state of being fully developed; the date a financial product is due
items.meaningCN: 成熟；成熟期；到期（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The bond reaches maturity next year.
items.exampleCN: 这只债券明年到期。

items.meaning: in a mature, calm, and considered way
items.meaningCN: 成熟地；深思熟虑地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: She responded maturely to the criticism.
items.exampleCN: 她对批评作出了成熟的回应。

items.meaning: not fully developed, or not behaving at an adult level
items.meaningCN: 未成熟的；幼稚的（im- 表示否定）
items.example: The fruit is still immature and should be left on the tree.
items.exampleCN: 果子还没成熟，应该留在树上。

items.meaningCN: 过早的；早产的（pre- 表示“在……之前”）
items.example: It is premature to announce a result.
items.exampleCN: 现在宣布结果还为时过早。

items.example: The adjective is the direct source of mature.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是 mature 的直接来源。

items.example: The stem appears in mature, maturity and maturation.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干见于 mature、maturity 与 maturation。

items.example: It forms maturity, the state of being ripe.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 maturity，即成熟状态。

items.example: It forms maturation, the process of ripening.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 maturation，即成熟过程。

items.meaning: the state of not being mature
items.example: The review criticized the immaturity of the plan.
items.exampleCN: 评审批评了这份计划的不成熟。

latinEntries.structure: Latin matutinus (of the morning) from mane (early)

latinEntries.meaning: the quality of happening or developing before the proper time
latinEntries.meaningCN: 过早；早产（在应有时间之前发生或发育的状态）

definition_zh: 成熟；成熟期；（金融票据、合同等的）到期；到期日
definition_en: the state of being fully developed; the point at which a financial instrument or contract falls due

senses.title: Biological maturity
senses.definition: the stage at which an organism can reproduce and its body has finished growing
senses.definitionCN: 生物能够繁殖、身体完成生长的阶段
senses.example: The seals reach sexual maturity at about four years old.
senses.exampleCN: 这些海豹大约四岁达到性成熟。
senses.why: Development has a natural end point, and the word names the moment when growth and reproduction are both available.
senses.whyCN: 发育有天然的终点，这个词命名的正是生长与繁殖都已具备的时刻。

senses.title: Emotional and judgemental maturity
senses.definition: the capacity to weigh consequences and act responsibly rather than impulsively
senses.definitionCN: 能权衡后果、负责任地行动而不凭冲动的能力
senses.example: The negotiations demanded patience and a certain maturity from both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判要求双方都有耐心与一定的成熟度。
senses.why: The same word for ripening is applied to character, because both describe something that has stopped being unripe.
senses.whyCN: 表示「成熟」的同一个词被用到性格上，因为两者都描述某物不再青涩。

senses.title: Ripeness of fruit or crops
senses.definition: the point at which a crop is ready to harvest, judged by colour, sugar or texture
senses.definitionCN: 作物达到可采收的程度，常以颜色、糖度或质地判断
senses.example: Growers test sugar levels to decide when the grapes reach maturity.
senses.exampleCN: 种植者测试糖度来决定葡萄何时成熟。
senses.why: Harvest timing needs a threshold, and the word names the stage where the fruit is fully formed and ready.
senses.whyCN: 采收时机需要一个阈值，这个词命名的就是果实完全成形且可用的阶段。

senses.title: A financial instrument falling due
senses.definition: the date on which a bond, note or loan must be repaid, or the state of having reached that date
senses.definitionCN: 债券、票据或贷款必须偿还的日期，或已到达该日期的状态
senses.example: The bond has a maturity of ten years from issue.
senses.exampleCN: 这只债券自发行起十年到期。
senses.why: Finance borrowed the language of ripening: a debt is mature when it has reached the point of payment.
senses.whyCN: 金融借用了「成熟」的说法：债务到了该偿付的时刻，就说它到期。

senses.title: The maturity date
senses.definition: the specific calendar day on which the principal of an instrument must be repaid
senses.definitionCN: 票据本金必须偿还的具体日期
senses.example: Investors marked the maturity date in their calendars.
senses.exampleCN: 投资者把到期日标在日历上。
senses.why: Once a date had to be written down, the abstract state became a fixed appointment.
senses.whyCN: 一旦必须写下一个日期，抽象状态就变成了固定的约定。

senses.title: Yield to maturity
senses.definition: the total return an investor receives if a bond is held until it matures
senses.definitionCN: 债券持有至到期时投资者获得的总回报率
senses.example: The bond's yield to maturity was higher than its coupon rate.
senses.exampleCN: 这只债券的到期收益率高于票面利率。
senses.why: The measure exists because the value of a bond depends on everything received up to and including the final day.
senses.whyCN: 这一指标之所以存在，是因为债券价值取决于到期日及之前收到的全部现金流。

senses.title: Expiry of a contract or policy
senses.definition: the end of the term for which an insurance policy or agreement runs
senses.definitionCN: 保险单或协议的有效期限结束
senses.example: The policy reached maturity and paid out a lump sum.
senses.exampleCN: 这份保单到期并支付了一笔一次性款项。
senses.why: Contracts also have a ripening point, after which the obligations are settled or renewed.
senses.whyCN: 合同同样有一个「熟透」的时点，此后义务结清或续约。

senses.title: Cellular and tissue maturation
senses.definition: the process by which unspecialised cells acquire their adult structure and function
senses.definitionCN: 未特化细胞获得成年结构与功能的过程
senses.example: The culture took three weeks to reach full maturity.
senses.exampleCN: 这组培养物用了三周才完全成熟。
senses.why: In cell biology maturity means differentiation is complete, so the word shifts from the whole body to a single lineage.
senses.whyCN: 在细胞生物学中，成熟意味着分化完成，这个词于是从整个身体转到单一细胞谱系。

senses.title: Soil and ecological maturity
senses.definition: the developed state of a soil profile or an ecosystem that has reached a stable community
senses.definitionCN: 土壤剖面发育完善，或生态系统达到稳定群落的状态
senses.example: The forest had reached maturity after a century without disturbance.
senses.exampleCN: 这片森林在百年无干扰之后达到成熟。
senses.why: Ecology applies the same arc from young to developed, treating a climax community as the mature end point.
senses.whyCN: 生态学套用同样的由幼到熟的弧线，把顶极群落视为成熟的终点。

intro.en: The word comes from Latin maturus, ripe or timely, and its noun maturitas. The Latin origin is clear; the exact date of the English noun's first use is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语中表示「成熟的、适时的」形容词及其名词形式。拉丁来源清楚，英语名词的确切首见年代为约数。

items.en: Maturus described fruit that had ripened and, by extension, anything that had come at the right time.
items.cn: 这个词先形容果实已经成熟，引申指任何「来得正是时候」的事物。

items.en: The same old root is thought to lie behind matutinus, of the morning, so ripeness and early hour share an idea of the right moment.
items.cn: 一般认为同一个古老词根也藏在表示「早晨的」形容词背后，因此「成熟」与「清晨」共享「恰当时刻」这一观念。

items.en: The abstract noun named the state of being ripe or timely, which English took over almost unchanged.
items.cn: 这个抽象名词指成熟或适时的状态，英语几乎原样借入。

items.en: English used the word first for physical ripeness and later for the due date of a debt.
items.cn: 英语先用它指生理成熟，后来才用于债务的到期。

items.en: As bills and bonds became standard instruments, maturity moved from the ripening of fruit to the day a payment falls due.
items.cn: 当票据与债券成为标准工具，「成熟」便从果实成熟转到付款到期的日子。

items.en: The financial use is dated to the modern banking era, but the precise first attestation of the noun is uncertain.
items.cn: 金融用法可系于现代银行时代，但该名词的确切首见时间不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the stem or the finance compounds; the second group names related states of completion.
note.cn: 第一组共享词干或金融搭配；第二组是表示「完成」的相关状态。

entries.definition: The adjective and verb meaning fully developed or to become so.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「成熟的」或「使成熟」的形容词与动词。

entries.definition: The process of becoming mature, especially in biology.
entries.definitionCN: 变为成熟的过程，尤用于生物学。

entries.definition: The state of not yet being mature.
entries.definitionCN: 尚未成熟的状态。

entries.definition: The day on which a financial instrument falls due.
entries.definitionCN: 金融工具到期的那一天。

entries.definition: The return earned by holding a bond to its due date.
entries.definitionCN: 持有债券至到期所获得的回报率。

entries.definition: The state of fruit being ready to eat or harvest.
entries.definitionCN: 果实可以食用或采收的状态。

entries.definition: The stage of being a fully grown person.
entries.definitionCN: 成为完全成年人的阶段。

entries.definition: The completion of growth or formation.
entries.definitionCN: 生长或形成的完成。

entries.definition: The date by which a payment or obligation must be met.
entries.definitionCN: 付款或义务必须履行的日期。

entries.definition: The end of the period for which something is valid.
entries.definitionCN: 某物有效的期限结束。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the arc from fruit to character to finance; abstract ones treat maturity as a threshold rather than a feeling.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着从果实到性格再到金融的弧线展开；抽象联想把成熟看作阈值而非感受。

normal.en: Maturity begins as a fruit word: colour, sugar, texture, ready to pick.
normal.cn: 成熟最初是果实词：颜色、糖度、质地，到了可采摘的程度。

normal.en: The same word then describes a person who can wait and weigh consequences.
normal.cn: 同一个词随后形容能等待、能权衡后果的人。

normal.en: In finance the fruit becomes a bond, and ripe means payable.
normal.cn: 在金融里，果实变成债券，「熟」就是「该付了」。

normal.en: A maturity date is the day the ripening is written into a calendar.
normal.cn: 到期日就是把「成熟」写进日历的那一天。

normal.en: Cells and soils mature too, because every system has a developed end state.
normal.cn: 细胞与土壤也会成熟，因为每个系统都有发育完成的状态。

abstract.en: Maturity is not an age, it is the point where something stops needing to be finished.
abstract.cn: 成熟不是年龄，而是某物不再需要被完成的那一刻。

abstract.en: Every field keeps the same fruit metaphor: unripe, ripening, due.
abstract.cn: 每个领域都保留同一个果实隐喻：未熟、将熟、到期。

abstract.en: A threshold can be crossed quietly, which is why maturity is often noticed only afterwards.
abstract.cn: 阈值可以悄无声息地被跨过，所以成熟往往事后才被察觉。

examples.en: The grapes reach maturity in late September.
examples.cn: 葡萄在九月下旬成熟。

examples.en: The bond has a maturity of five years.
examples.cn: 这只债券期限五年。

examples.en: Emotional maturity matters more than age in this role.
examples.cn: 在这个岗位上，情感成熟比年龄更重要。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「马球里提」——果子熟了才敢办「马球赛」，晚了就到期了：成熟、到期

root: 来自拉丁语 maturus「成熟的、适时的」及其名词 maturitas，经法语进入英语。一般认为表示「早晨的」拉丁形容词也出自同一古老词根，因此「成熟」与「恰当时刻」共享一个观念。金融「到期」义属现代银行时代的引申，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses grow from one image of ripening: the body, the character, the crop, the debt, the date, the return, the contract, the cell and the soil.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都从一个「成熟」意象长出来：身体、性格、作物、债务、日期、回报、合同、细胞与土壤。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sugar meter, a rising curve, a crate waiting at the end of the row.
core.cn: 核心意象：糖度计、上升的曲线、地头等着的果筐。

branches.en: THE RIPENING CORE: body and crop both arrive at the point of being fully formed.
branches.cn: 成熟内核：身体与作物都到达完全成形的时点。

branches.en: THE CHARACTER: the same threshold applied to judgement and patience.
branches.cn: 性格层面：同一阈值被用到判断力与耐心上。

branches.en: THE FINANCIAL ARC: due, the date of due, and the return earned by waiting for it.
branches.cn: 金融弧线：到期、到期日，以及等到期所获的回报。

branches.en: THE OTHER COMPLETIONS: a contract's term ends, a cell's differentiation finishes.
branches.cn: 其他完成形态：合同期限结束，细胞分化完成。

branches.en: THE ECOLOGICAL END: a soil profile or a community reaches its developed state.
branches.cn: 生态终点：土壤剖面或群落达到发育完成的状态。

intro.en: The word is a Latin adjective plus an abstract noun ending, with English relatives built by negation and by prefixes of time.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁形容词加抽象名词词尾，英语亲属词由否定与时间前缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the adjective of ripeness, its abstract noun and the verb of ripening; English adds the ending -ity and the negative and anticipatory prefixes.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了表示成熟的形容词、抽象名词与使成熟的动词；英语加上表示性质的词尾，以及否定与提前的前缀。

items.example: It described fruit at the right moment and then any timely thing.
items.exampleCN: 它先形容恰当时刻的果实，后指任何适时之物。

items.example: The abstract noun passed into English almost unchanged.
items.exampleCN: 这个抽象名词几乎原样进入英语。

items.example: The verb supplies the English process noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供了英语的过程名词与动词。

items.example: It turns the adjective into the name of a state.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成状态名称。

items.example: The shorter form drops the abstract ending.
items.exampleCN: 较短的形容词形式去掉了抽象词尾。

items.example: The ending marks an ongoing process rather than a state.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记进行中的过程而非状态。

items.example: It forms the adjective and noun for what has not ripened.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「尚未成熟」的形容词与名词。

items.example: It marks a birth or event that comes before the due time.
items.exampleCN: 它标记早于应有时刻的出生或事件。

definition_zh: 使最大化；使增至最大；充分利用；把……发挥到极致
definition_en: to make something as great, large, or effective as it can possibly be
core_image: 把一只旋钮拧到刻度盘最右端、直到再也拧不动的顶点
scene: 这里指「使最大化」。 The plant manager turned every dial to its limit to maximize output before the export deadline.
sceneCN: 这里 maximize 是「把产量推到最高」（第 3 个义项：把产出、效率推到最高）；句意：出口截止日前，厂长把每一个旋钮都拧到极限，以把产量推到最高。场景要点：车间里的控制台、一排拧到头的旋钮、堆到天花板的成品箱。
